title: Implement health-envelope and readiness quorum hysteresis to stabilize autoscaling
creator: Aisha Navarro
description: Problem: Flapping autoscaler and noisy failovers during cross-region incidents. Current readiness/liveness checks are binary and tightly coupled to transient errors, which causes rapid scale-outs and repeated cross-region failover decisions that burn error budget and spike costs. Goal: introduce a ‘health envelope’ abstraction plus a readiness quorum with hysteresis to make scaling decisions robust to transient noise while preserving fast failover when an entire region degrades.
acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler scales fewer than 2x times during synthetic transient error bursts (10m window) in lab runs
Regional failover triggers only after readiness-quorum is violated for a configurable hysteresis window (default 60s)
New metrics available in Console: health_envelope_score (0-100), readiness_quorum_ratio, autoscaler_cooling_state
Canary rollout to a subset of services reduces inter-region thrash in staged traffic test by >= 40% vs baseline
tasks: Design health envelope model: combine liveness, readiness, synthetic transaction latency, and error-rate into single score
Implement readiness quorum service in control plane and expose per-region weightings
Add hysteresis controller for scaling/failover decisions (configurable windows and dampening factors)
Integrate with autoscaler: replace immediate-probe-based triggers with envelope thresholds and cooling timers
Create synthetic warmup probe generator for gradual scale transitions
Add end-to-end tests and chaos scenarios (region partial network loss, API latency spikes, token storm)
Dashboard panels and alerting: error-budget burn, envelope drift, quorum violations, cooling events
Run staged canary across non-prod -> preprod -> 10% prod traffic and capture SLO impact
comments: 2026-02-16 - Aisha Navarro: Kickoff meeting notes: agreed to favor a continuous health score over binary probes. Decided to prototype envelope using weighted percentiles (p50/p95) for latency plus 5m error-rate and liveness failures.

2026-02-22 - Mateo Chen: Prototype implementation added: health_envelope_score computed in control plane. Early experiment shows smoothing window of 45s reduces scale-outs during short spikes. Pushed draft PR for feedback.

2026-02-25 - Priya Rao (SRE): Reviewed prototype. Concern: a single global smoothing window may delay failover when region is down. Proposal: quorum-based decision where regional scores contribute weighted votes, and a region-wide knockout overrides quorum if all nodes report critical failure.

2026-03-02 - Mateo Chen: Implemented readiness_quorum and hysteresis parameters (window, cooling_factor). Added configuration per deployment to tune for latency-sensitive vs throughput-oriented services.
2026-03-05 - Elena Gutierrez (PM): Request to expose as feature-flagged rollout so customers on Dedicated can opt-in during migration. Also capture telemetry for 90 days for regression analysis.

2026-03-07 - Load test results: simulated token storm (50k req/s) in single region. Baseline autoscaler triggered 6 scale events in 10 minutes; with envelope + hysteresis it triggered 2 and maintained P99 latency within SLO for 85% of requests.
2026-03-10 - Security review note: no changes to customer data plane. Control plane decisioning only; KMS review not required. Confirmed by Security (Ben Wallace).
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-damping could delay real failover and increase error budget burn. Mitigation: add critical-failure path where unanimous region critical liveness triggers immediate failover regardless of hysteresis.
Risk: Too many configuration knobs cause operational confusion. Mitigation: provide three opinionated profiles (latency-sensitive, throughput, conservative) and guardrails in Console UX.
Risk: Observability gap during rollout. Mitigation: increase retention for envelope metrics during canary and add automated regression tests that fail the rollout if SLOs degrade beyond thresholds.
